note: Polite आप form throughout. Buttons and menu items use the polite imperative as in Windows/Office Hindi: खोलें, सहेजें, बंद करें, हटाएँ. Labels and headings are nouns.

Sentences end with the purna viram । (not a period); ? ! : , … and “ ” as in English. Keep … on menu items that open a dialog. No Title Case. Use nukta (फ़ाइल, ज़ूम) and chandrabindu (हाँ, जाँच, हटाएँ).
Units, ×, %, keys (Ctrl, Shift, Esc, F1) and abbreviations stay in Latin script as written. No space before % in Hindi.
Hindi has nplurals=2, plural=(n > 1): the first form also serves 0, so both forms must show {n}. Verbs and nouns agree: 1 स्लाइड खोली गई / 3 स्लाइडें खोली गईं.
Bare {} placeholders cannot be reordered: write “X of Y” with two bare {} as “{} (कुल {})”, never “{} में से {}”. Named ones ({n}, {shown}) may move: {n} में से {shown}.
When {} is a file or slide name, use को / का constructions (default masculine verb) so the sentence is grammatical whatever the name: {} को सहेजा गया, {} का निर्यात किया गया.
Hours, minutes, seconds in compact times: 1 घं॰ 02 मि॰, 4 मि॰ 05 से॰ (with the abbreviation sign ॰, so से॰ is not read as the postposition से).
